title: Normal local completions over a quasi-excellent closed fibre
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and assume $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] and $A/I$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the maximal-ideal-adic completion $\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}=\varprojlim_n A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p^n A_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is a normal local domain. No universal catenarity or G-ring hypothesis on $A$ is assumed.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1 Step 1 (1-4), printed p.8, invoking Nishimura–Nishimura Theorem A (lifting of Nagata Z-rings); normal rings with geometrically normal formal fibres have normal completions. Applied also in (5.3), printed p.9. This is the normal-completion consequence of the weaker Z-ring lifting theorem, not Theorem 5.1 itself.

proof.text: Put $Q=A/I$. By [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata], $Q$ is Nagata. By [def-exc-excellent-ring] it is a G-ring. For every prime of $Q$, [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] says that each formal fibre of its local completion is geometrically regular: after every finite purely inseparable extension of its residue field the fibre is a Noetherian regular ring. Each such ring is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. This verifies exactly $N(Q)$ in the lifting lemma, without any assertion about formal fibres of $A$ yet.

source.place: Tags 07QV, lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata; 07QT, definition-excellent; 07GH, definition-G-ring. For regular-implies-normal: algebra.tex Tag 0567, lemma-regular-normal. Normal-fibre preparation in Kurano–Shimomoto Step 1 (1-4).

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-nagata-normal-formal-fibres-lifting] to the original pair $(A,I)$: Noetherianity and $I$-adic completeness are hypotheses, and Step 1 supplies both quotient conditions. Obtain $N(A)$. In particular, for any prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, all fibre rings of $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}$ are normal: take the identity (finite purely inseparable) residue-field extension in $N(A)$. The theorem applies to $(A,I)$, not to the possibly incomplete localization.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 1 (1-4), printed p.8; Appendix A, Definition A.1(1) and the Nagata Z-ring row, printed pp.14–15, quoting Nishimura–Nishimura, Ideal-adic completion of Noetherian rings II, Theorem A.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak p$ and put $B=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $C=\widehat B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], $B$ is a Noetherian normal domain. Applying the latter also to each further prime localization makes $B$ a normal ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $C$ is Noetherian and local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pBC$ and nonzero residue field $B/\mathfrak pB$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], $B\to C$ is flat.

source.place: Tags 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; 00GY, lemma-localize-normal-domain; 0316, lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian; 05GI, lemma-radical-completion and 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated; 00MC, lemma-completion-faithfully-flat.

proof.text: The two Noetherian rings $B,C$, the flat map of Step 3, the normal base $B$, and every normal fibre from Step 2 meet all five hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal]. Thus $C$ is a normal ring.

source.place: Tag 0C22, lemma-normal-goes-up-noetherian; also more-algebra.tex Tag 0C23, lemma-completion-normal-local-ring.

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak n$ be the maximal ideal of $C$. By [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $C_{\mathfrak n}$ is a normal domain. Every denominator outside $\mathfrak n$ is a unit in the local ring $C$, so $c/s\mapsto cs^{-1}$ is an inverse to $C\to C_{\mathfrak n}$. Hence $C$ itself is a normal local domain. The prime $\mathfrak p$ was arbitrary.

Kurano–Shimomoto kurano40.pdf (not under literature/; fetched read-only, text extracted in /tmp): Thm 5.1 (1-3) and (1-4) p.8, §2 Z-ring := [12, Def (0.1)], App. A Def A.1(1) and table p.15 (LP for Nagata = Marot; LP for Nagata Z-ring = Nishimura–Nishimura Theorem A). Geometric normality checked with Stacks 037Z/0380 (finite purely inseparable form; no Noetherian hypothesis). The item is exactly the (1-4) inference: normal domain + Z-ring ⇒ Â_P normal local domain. Arbitrary I is fine because the LP is general. Steps: (1) QE ⇒ Nagata by 07QV, G-ring regular fibres normal by 0567, so N(Q) holds. (2) The new node is applied to the complete pair (A,I), not to A_p; the identity extension gives normal fibres. (3) 00FN, 00GY, 0316, 05GI/05GG, 00MC: B is a Noetherian normal ring, C Noetherian local, B→C flat. (4) All 5 hypotheses of 0C22 matched. (5) Local normal ring = normal domain. Edge cases checked: p=0, I=0, I=A, nonnormal A, char 0 vs char p. The item is reachable from nt-target via the qe-normal-counterexample-reduction chain. No circularity: the QE lifting nodes are downstream. No SGA.
